newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dublin Greenpeace office to close on cash worries.
newsitem.headline: Dublin Greenpeace office to close on cash worries.

text.p: The international environmental pressure group Greenpeace is to close its Dublin office for financial reasons, executive director Thilo Dode told Reuters on Thursday.
He said the group was reviewing its representation world wide and had decided to close the Dublin office, which was officially opened in 1991.
The Dublin office played a major role in informing public opionion about Britain's Sellafield nuclear reprocessing facility across the Irish sea, he said.
But we have to consider what funds are going to various offices across the world. Keeping Dublin open for three years would cost around 350,000 dollars," he said.
Greenpeace has 33 offices worldwide and is currently considering opening a branch in Hong Kong.
